original_test_intent: Verify that Restore Defaults loads the platform-defined BIOS default profile and that the resulting configuration can be saved, without losing the ability to restore the approved operational profile.
original_method: Use the interactive Save & Exit page to invoke Restore Defaults, save the resulting settings, collect captures and logs, and compare the applied values and system health with the platform's defined defaults.
manual_activity: A human must select Restore Defaults, review the pending full-profile changes, save them through the firmware UI and observe the firmware result. Agent-side readback cannot substitute for this control-path acceptance.
required_inputs: Board/BIOS identity and documented default profile
BMC/OOB recovery, stable power and maintenance window
safety_requirements: Treat Restore Defaults as a whole-profile mutation, not a single setting change.
Capture boot, storage, security, performance and management settings before activation.
Confirm defaults will not strand the host or recovery path.
Use one-authorized-user approval for the complete unchanged plan.
Stop on loss of boot/storage/management access or undocumented default deltas.
Restore the approved operational profile and do not retry automatically.
agent_execution_scope: Collect read-only platform identity, baseline, configuration comparisons and health/log evidence.
Flag deviations from the supplied default matrix and incomplete restoration.
Do not operate firmware UI, approve full-profile changes or set PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the default-load/save plan, expected matrix and recovery boundary.
Perform and capture Restore Defaults, save/activation and operational-profile restoration.
Assess default conformity and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Correctly states there is no agent command equivalent for the interactive control. Its added save and boot checks are reasonable execution details but must follow the platform's documented activation behavior.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain Restore Defaults through the actual firmware UI; use read-only export or management telemetry only as supporting evidence, never as a replacement for the control under test.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Restore Defaults, no-script state and 5/5-minute fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Export or capture the complete pre-test profile, invoke Restore Defaults manually, save/activate as documented, compare every available field with the approved default matrix, verify boot/storage/security/management health, then restore and re-verify the operational profile.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact board and BIOS release under test.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BIOS/BMC versions and configuration-export format/version.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform BIOS setup and default-profile documentation supplied for the project.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Turns a generic function check into a full-profile before/default/final state trace.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Expands observability without replacing or narrowing the source action.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Default matrix, baseline, activation semantics, recovery and restoration owner.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Undocumented dynamic or hidden defaults may require owner disposition rather than inferred acceptance.

project_override_considerations: The project may define which documented profile, activation path and health checks apply, but must record any excluded or intentionally restored fields and cannot claim a generic factory-default result without the comparison evidence.
expected_evidence: Identity, approval, documented default matrix and recovery plan
Field-level default comparison plus boot/storage/security/management health
Restored operational profile, final health, logs and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The criterion that the setting can be saved is terse but can coherently mean saving the default profile loaded by Restore Defaults. It is an underspecified acceptance condition, not the opposite of the named function.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The operation is identifiable. Missing default values, recovery details and project health scope are execution-readiness inputs rather than an unresolved operation semantic.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Agrees with the manual boundary and retains its full-profile and bootability concerns while making platform activation semantics explicit.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its complete baseline/default/restoration controls and clarifies that missing project documentation does not permanently block the library case.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates automation classification from readiness and formal engineer verdict while defining field-level evidence.

review_improvement: Makes the blast radius and restoration obligation explicit and prevents one visible setting from being used as proof that the whole default profile loaded correctly.
independent_technical_reasoning: Restore Defaults acts on many NVRAM fields and its acceptance requires an interactive firmware control plus human review of the resulting state. Supporting exports may accelerate comparison, but the core action and observation remain MANUAL ONLY.
no_automatic_retry: Do not invoke Restore Defaults or save again automatically after any unexpected field, activation or health result; preserve the full delta and obtain engineer disposition.
